description: A weekend escalation from a customer executive, sent to a shared alias rather than to the user directly, with the user named only in the body. Tests that recipient-based heuristics do not lose an item that is unambiguously the user's by content.

events.context_label: Escalation — invoicing errors ahead of Monday's board pack
events.text: To the account team: we have found three duplicate line items across our last two invoices, totalling roughly 18,000. Our finance director has to submit the board pack on Monday afternoon and cannot sign off numbers he does not trust. Wes, you are our account manager, so I am asking you directly here: I need either corrected invoices or a written explanation of the discrepancy before Monday midday. If neither arrives I will have to raise this with your VP, which I would prefer not to do.

Saw the Vantage Grid escalation land in the alias. I can pull the invoice history but I can't authorise a credit note or speak for the account, so this needs Wes on Monday morning. Flagging so it doesn't sit.

Update from the invoice history: two of the three duplicates are real, both from the May usage import. The third is not a duplicate, it's a genuine second environment they added in June. So the number is closer to 11,000 than 18,000.

Weekend note for account managers: credit notes requested before 10:00 Monday are issued the same day. After that it's 48 hours. The requester must be the named account manager; we cannot accept these from colleagues.
Reminder the team lunch is Wednesday not Tuesday. Nobody needs to do anything, just turn up hungry.

pending_items.description: Get corrected invoices or a written explanation of the duplicate line items to Rosalind at Vantage Grid before Monday midday, ahead of their board pack — she has said she will otherwise escalate to the VP.

Request the credit note yourself before 10:00 Monday for same-day issue — billing will not accept the request from a colleague, and after 10:00 it takes 48 hours, which misses the customer's Monday-midday deadline.

ground_truth.notes: The email is addressed to a shared alias, so any rule of the form 'is the user in the To line' fails, while the body names the user and states the obligation as directly as it is possible to state one. Two pending items rather than one, and the second is only discoverable by joining two artifacts: the customer's midday deadline is unreachable unless the credit note request goes in before 10:00, and only the user can file it. That inference is the real test here — a system that lists the customer email alone leaves the user to discover the 10:00 constraint themselves. Bo's correction is a precision trap in the opposite direction: the customer's 18,000 figure is wrong and repeating it as established fact is a fabricated claim, even though the customer said it, because the fixture contains the refutation. The social post is filler that must not appear as an item.
